bounds: One user message posted in a task room with one to three live sub-agents bound to it (labels Ada, Bob and Cy), each either in the middle of a turn or ready. The message is an explicit stop, a course correction or a plain instruction, and it names no sub-agent, names one sub-agent's label, @-mentions one sub-agent's label, carries a connector mention the room cannot map to a sub-agent, or @-mentions a handle that is no sub-agent's label. The classifier model answers in prose, so decideInterruption decides from the text. The conformance script replays every generated message through createActiveSessionForwardHandler on a PGlite-backed runtime and requires all 330 room, turn-state, address and intent combinations (30 with one sub-agent, 84 with two, 216 with three). Classifier verdicts, additive or code-instruction stops, labels outside ASCII, messages that name several sub-agents, shared origin channels and Eliza participants with a shouldRespond verdict are not covered by this model. Under weak fairness of the forward step every bound sub-agent eventually gets its outcome. Explicit stuttering lets the classifier call stay pending, so the same claim without fairness must fail. No time bound is proved.

assumptions: A continuously enabled forward step eventually runs (weak fairness). This checks that every bound sub-agent then gets its outcome, not how long the classifier call takes.
No fairness is assumed. The classifier call may stay pending forever, so a temporal loop counterexample is required.
